title: The Rs 3.2 Lakh Crore Capex Pipeline: Who Owns the CFO Forecast?
subtitle: RBI Bulletin of 25 September 2026 puts Q1 FY27 GDP at 7.8 percent, August CPI at 4.8 percent, and private corporate pipeline capex at Rs 3.2 lakh crore for 2026-27. A composite industrial CFO must decide which projects stay in the sanctioned list before the October board.
category: Capital Budgeting, Private Investment & CFO Judgment
description: HBS-style teaching case dated 26 September 2026. Public facts from the Reserve Bank of India Bulletin released 25 September 2026: Q1:2026-27 real GDP growth 7.8 percent; headline CPI 4.8 percent in August; merchandise trade deficit narrowed on strong exports; FX reserves at an all-time high; system liquidity surplus surged after FCNR(B) deposit flows. Bulletin article on private corporate investment estimates envisaged capex of Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 from the pipeline across financing channels. August 2026 MPC held the LAF repo at 5.25 percent with a neutral stance. Composite firm: Kalinga Heavy Systems Ltd. Composite decision-maker: CFO Arjun Sen.
thumbnail: RS 3.2 LAKH CRORE IS IN THE PIPELINE. WHICH PROJECTS DOES YOUR BOARD KEEP?
sources: Reserve Bank of India, RBI Bulletin – September 2026, press release dated 25 September 2026. Articles: State of the Economy; Credit-Deposit Divergence: A Balance Sheet Decomposition; Private Corporate Investment: Growth in 2025-26 and Outlook for 2026-27.

RBI Bulletin September 2026, State of the Economy: Q1:2026-27 real GDP growth 7.8 percent; headline inflation 4.8 percent in August; trade deficit narrowed; FX reserves at an all-time high; liquidity surplus after FCNR(B) flows.
RBI Bulletin September 2026, Private Corporate Investment article: envisaged capex estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 from the phasing profile of pipeline projects across financing channels.

RBI Monetary Policy Committee, August 3–5 2026: policy repo held at 5.25 percent; SDF 5.00 percent; MSF and Bank Rate 5.50 percent; stance neutral. Real GDP 2026-27 projected 6.7 percent at the August meeting; CPI 2026-27 projected 5.0 percent.
RBI press materials: West Asia geopolitical tensions cited as a source of energy-price and market volatility in the September 2026 Bulletin.
